India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Raipur man buys Rs 1 crore insurance policy, dies of cardiac arrest 15 months later, insurer refuses wife's claim over other policies, consumer commission orders Rs 1 crore payout with Rs 1.15 lakh co
Article Text:
(AI image) A District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission found Aditya Birla Sun Life Insurance guilty of unfair trade practices.

Key highlights

Woman's husband buys a Rs 1 crore life insurance policy in September 2018 but dies of cardiac arrest in December 2019.

Insurer rejects wife's death claim, alleging the deceased had failed to disclose multiple other life insurance policies.

Raipur consumer commission rejects the insurer's defence, observing that it had an opportunity to verify the deceased's existing insurance coverage before issuing the policy.

Commission holds the insurer guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practices, directing it to pay Rs 1 crore with Rs 1 lakh compensation and Rs 15,000 litigation expenses.

Insurer directed to make the payment within 45 days, failing which it will have to pay 7% annual interest until payment.





RAIPUR: Holding an insurance company guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practices, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Additional Bench, Raipur, has directed the insurer to pay a death insurance claim of Rs 1 crore to a woman whose husband died of cardiac arrest in Dec, 2019.The commission held that the insurance company's failure to honour the death claim, despite the policy being in force and the death having occurred during its validity, amounted to deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.The commission, comprising president Prashant Kundu and member Dr Anand Vergese, passed the order on Nov 3, while allowing a complaint filed by Chanda Pincha against insurance company.Apart from the Rs 1 crore insurance amount, the commission directed the company to pay Rs 1 lakh as compensation for mental and physical agony suffered by the complainant and Rs 15,000 towards litigation expenses.The entire amount has to be paid within forty-five days. In case of failure to comply with the order within the stipulated period, the insurer will also have to pay interest at 7% per annum until payment.According to the complaint, Chanda's husband, Pawan Pincha, a director of a private company, had purchased a policy, bearing number 007644841, on Sept 10, 2018.The policy provided a death cover of Rs 1 crore for the primary insured, Pawan, while his wife was the secondary insured with a cover of Rs 50 lakh.The policy had a tenure of 39 years, with maturity scheduled for Sept 10, 2057. The complainant's husband had paid a premium of Rs 36,969.40.Pawan died of a sudden cardiac arrest on Dec 21, 2019. Following his death, his wife, being the nominee, submitted a claim for the assured amount of Rs 1 crore. However, the insurance company rejected the claim on March 17, 2020, alleging that the deceased had failed to disclose several other life insurance policies taken from different insurance companies.The insurer maintained that the deceased had obtained multiple life insurance policies, including policies with substantial sums assured, without disclosing the relevant details in the proposal form. It argued that the suppression of material information amounted to a violation of the insurance contract and justified repudiation of the claim.The company also challenged the maintainability of the complaint, contending that the commission lacked territorial and pecuniary jurisdiction. It further alleged that the complainant had not impleaded the concerned insurance agent as a party to the proceedings.However, the commission, after examining the complaint, affidavits, insurance documents, medical records and correspondence between the parties, rejected the insurer's objections.The commission observed that the insurer had issued the policy after receiving the proposal and premium, and had an opportunity to examine the deceased's existing insurance coverage before accepting the proposal.It noted that the deceased had held other life insurance policies, but the insurer had failed to establish that the complainant was responsible for any concealment or that the circumstances justified repudiating the death claim.The order also referred to the fact that claims under certain other insurance policies held by the deceased had been settled by the respective insurance companies, while the claim under the disputed policy was rejected.It consequently directed the company to release the Rs 1 crore death benefit to the complainant, along with compensation and litigation expenses, within 45 days.
Article Summary: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission found Aditya Birla Sun Life Insurance guilty of unfair trade practices. Woman's husband buys a Rs 1 crore life insurance policy in September 2018 but dies of cardiac arrest in December 2019. Insurer rejects wife's death claim, alleging the deceased had failed to disclose multiple other life insurance policies.

Article Title: Gwalior family finds iron blade inside Dettol soap after child suffers cheek cut; consumer commission orders Reckitt India to pay Rs 50,000, shopkeeper and distributor Rs 2,000 each
Article Text:
AI Image Used For Representational Purpose Only





BHOPAL: A complaint over a blade found inside a Dettol soap bar has resulted in a Rs 54,000 compensation order against the manufacturer, distributor and retailer, after a Gwalior consumer commission held that inadequate quality checks had exposed a child to a potential health hazard.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Gwalior, passed the order on November 17, partly allowing a complaint filed by Angad Singh Tomar against Mohit Kirana Store, the soap distributor and Reckitt (India) Ltd, the manufacturer of Dettol soap.According to the complaint, Tomar purchased a Dettol soap bar from Mohit Kirana Store on May 21, 2025. While his minor son was using it during a bath, a sharp cut appeared on the child’s cheek. On examining the soap, the family found an iron blade embedded inside it.Tomar approached the shopkeeper with the complaint, following which the retailer replaced the soap bar. However, the family was shocked to find another blade inside the replacement bar as well.The complainant subsequently lodged a complaint with the National Consumer Helpline on May 27, 2025, alleging that the matter had not been satisfactorily resolved.He later approached the consumer commission on June 17, 2025, seeking Rs 3.5 lakh as compensation for physical and mental harassment, besides Rs 50,000 towards litigation expenses.The retailer argued that he was merely selling the soap and had purchased it from the distributor. The manufacturer, meanwhile, maintained that stringent quality-control procedures were followed during production, including the use of two metal detectors to identify and remove foreign metal particles.The company also claimed that it had purchased 21 soap bars from the same batch through the retailer and subjected 14 of them to testing at an FDA-recognised laboratory, where no defect was detected. It suggested that the blade could have been deliberately inserted into the soap.However, the commission observed that the manufacturer had failed to produce evidence establishing that the particular soap bar supplied to the complainant had undergone the claimed quality checks. It also noted that there was no proof of inspection after the soap was frozen, packed and made ready for sale.The panel observed that merely testing other soap bars from the same batch did not establish that the defective bar was free of foreign material. It also rejected the manufacturer’s suggestion that the complainant might have deliberately inserted the blade, observing that no credible evidence had been produced to support the allegation.In its final order dated November 17, 2026, the commission directed Reckitt (India) Ltd to pay Rs 50,000 compensation to the complainant within 45 days. The retailer and distributor were each directed to pay Rs 2,000. The manufacturer was also ordered to pay Rs 2,000 towards litigation expenses. A 6% annual interest will apply to the compensation amounts if payment is delayed beyond the stipulated period.The complaint was thus partly allowed, with the commission holding the manufacturer liable for deficiency in service and the retailer and distributor responsible for their respective lapses.
Article Summary: Angad Singh Tomar purchased a Dettol soap bar from Mohit Kirana Store on May 21, 2025. While his minor son was using it during a bath, a sharp cut appeared on the child’s cheek. On examining the soap, the family found an iron blade embedded inside it.

Article Title: 580kg giant marlin draws hundreds to Koti Chennaya Fish Centre in Ujire, as passengers, schoolchildren and residents stop for a closer look
Article Text:
The fish was so large that a crane was required to load it at Malpe harbour before it was transported to Ujire in a goods vehicle.





MANGALURU: A 580-kg giant ‘Madal’ (marlin) brought to Koti Chennaya Fish Centre became an unusual attraction on Friday, drawing passengers, schoolchildren, passers-by and curious residents. Many also lined up to buy the prized fish.Passengers on buses passing through Ujire turned their heads towards the shop, while schoolchildren and passers-by stopped for a closer look. Proprietor Nagesh said the crowd numbered at least 400-500, with many visiting just to see the fish.The fish was so large that a crane was required to load it at Malpe harbour before it was transported to Ujire in a goods vehicle. Nagesh said the fish is considered a delicacy for its taste and flesh with very few bones.This is the fourth time such a large fish has been brought to the shop. Nagesh said the 580-kg fish was the biggest of its kind he had brought to Ujire so far. The previous largest fish brought by the shop weighed 525 kg and arrived last year.Nagesh said he regularly procures large-sized fish and has built a customer base for such varieties. “We are among the few in Dakshina Kannada who take up the buy of such large fish,” he said.
Article Summary: A 580-kg giant ‘Madal’ (marlin) brought to Koti Chennaya Fish Centre became an unusual attraction. The fish was so large that a crane was required to load it at Malpe harbour before it was transported to Ujire in a goods vehicle.

Article Title: UP man takes SBI home loan in 1997, repays it in 2019; bank fails to return original deed for 7 years, consumer commission orders Rs 5,000 daily penalty and Rs 10,000 costs
Article Text:
Image Used For Representational Only





LUCKNOW: An elderly man in Aligarh had to approach the consumer commission after the State Bank of India (SBI) failed to return his original property deed for seven years despite the closure of his home loan. Holding the bank guilty of deficiency in service, the Aligarh District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has directed it to hand over the document and pay compensation of Rs 5,000 for every day of delay, calculated from the date the loan was repaid until the deed is returned.The complainant, Gulveer Singh Chauhan, 70, a resident of Gyan Sarovar Colony, had taken a home loan from SBI's City Branch in Baradwari in 1997. As security for the loan, he deposited the original sale deed (document number 7134), dated December 18, 1997, with the bank. Chauhan cleared the entire outstanding loan on May 13, 2019, following which the bank issued him a no-dues certificate. However, his repeated requests for the return of the original property papers did not yield any result. The bank reportedly told him that it was unable to trace the deed.The absence of the original document created problems for Chauhan in dealing with his property.He said he faced difficulties in establishing ownership, transferring the house and securing another loan from a different bank. With the matter unresolved, he filed a consumer complaint on June 13, 2023. During the proceedings, SBI acknowledged that Chauhan had taken a loan and deposited the original deed with it, but contested his complaint, describing it as false.The commission also examined a letter issued by the bank on February 13, 2020. It confirmed that the loan account had been closed on May 13, 2019, with no outstanding dues. The bench, comprising commission chairman Hasnain Qureshi and member Purnima Singh Rajput, observed that the bank's failure to return the original property document after receiving full repayment amounted to a deficiency in service.In its order, the commission directed SBI to return the original sale deed and pay Chauhan Rs 5,000 per day from May 13, 2019, until the document is handed over. The bank has also been asked to pay Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses. It has been given 45 days to comply with the directions. Failure to implement the order could invite prosecution under Section 72 of the Consumer Protection Act.
Article Summary: Gulveer Singh Chauhan, 70, had taken a home loan from SBI's City Branch in Baradwari in 1997. As security for the loan, he deposited the original sale deed with the bank. Chauhan cleared the entire outstanding loan on May 13, 2019, following which the bank issued him a no-dues certificate.

Article Title: Chandigarh man pays Rs 4,620 for 6 extra-legroom seats on Mumbai flight, 4 friends get different seats; consumer commission raises compensation from Rs 9,000 to Rs 30,000, orders refund with 9% intere
Article Text:
AI Image Used For Representational Purpose Only





CHANDIGARH: A seat upgrade for two passengers did little to make up for an airline's failure to honour the paid reservations of four others travelling with them. Vineet Khurana had spent Rs 4,620 to secure six extra-legroom seats on a Chandigarh-Mumbai flight, but four members of his group were shifted to different seats when they boarded. The Chandigarh State Consumer Commission has now raised the compensation payable by the airline from Rs 9,000 to Rs 30,000, holding that a refund alone could not compensate for the inconvenience.Khurana had booked tickets for himself, his wife and four friends on a flight scheduled for January 16, 2023. On January 12, he paid an additional Rs 4,620 to reserve six specific extra-legroom seats for the group. However, when they received their boarding passes, the seat numbers did not match their reservations. Khurana and his wife were upgraded to Premium Economy, while the other four passengers were assigned different seats as the flight was fully booked. Khurana later learnt that the seats he had paid for had allegedly been allotted to other passengers.He raised the issue with the airline, which acknowledged its lapse in an email dated February 9, 2023, and offered to refund the additional Rs 4,620. Khurana declined the offer.The airline subsequently offered him a Rs 500 voucher on February 20.Khurana then approached the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, alleging deficiency in service and unfair trade practice. He sought compensation for the inconvenience, mental agony and harassment caused by the failure to provide the confirmed seats. On March 2, 2026, the district commission partly allowed his complaint. It directed the airline to refund Rs 4,620 with 9% annual simple interest from the date of payment and pay Rs 9,000 as consolidated compensation for mental agony, harassment and litigation expenses.Dissatisfied with the compensation, Khurana appealed before the Chandigarh State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, seeking an enhancement of the amount. The commission observed that upgrading Khurana and his wife did not absolve the airline of its responsibility towards the four other passengers who were denied their booked seats.It noted that passengers may choose extra-legroom seats for reasons beyond personal preference, including their body structure, physical comfort and convenience. The group had made advance arrangements and paid additional charges to secure these seats, but four members were not provided the facility. The commission also took note of the embarrassment Khurana faced at the airport in front of his companions. It said returning the additional amount could not reverse the inconvenience and mental distress caused by the airline's failure to honour the reservations. The Rs 500 voucher offered by the airline was considered a nominal gesture rather than adequate compensation.The state commission held that the Rs 9,000 awarded by the district commission was on the lower side. Referring to established principles laid down by the Supreme Court and the National Consumer Commission, it said compensation should be fair and proportionate to the deficiency in service and the injury suffered, as there was no fixed formula for determining the amount. In its November 13 order, the commission enhanced the consolidated compensation for mental agony, harassment and litigation expenses from Rs 9,000 to Rs 30,000.It retained the direction to refund Rs 4,620 with 9% annual simple interest from the date of payment. The airline must comply within 45 days of receiving the certified copy of the order. If it fails to do so, the awarded amounts will attract 12% annual simple interest after the expiry of the 45-day period until realisation.
Article Summary: Vineet Khurana had spent Rs 4,620 to secure six extra-legroom seats on a Chandigarh-Mumbai flight. Four members of his group were shifted to different seats when they boarded. The airline acknowledged its lapse in an email dated February 9, 2023, and offered to refund the additional £4,620. But the state commission held that a refund alone could not compensate for the inconvenience.

Article Title: Kupwara man billed Rs 2,10,934 for electricity over joint family's old dues; consumer commission quashes bill, directs KPDCL to issue fresh one and pay Rs 10,000 litigation charges
Article Text:
AI Generated Image Used For Representational Purpose Only





SRINAGAR: The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Kupwara , has quashed an electricity bill of Rs 2,10,934 issued by the Kashmir Power Distribution Corporation Limited (KPDCL) to a resident of Drugmulla in frontier district of Kupwara, directing the KPDCL to issue a fresh bill for his newly constructed house and pay Rs 10,000 as litigation charges.The commission, comprising president Peerzada Qousar Hussain and member Nyla Yaseen, last week partly allowed a complaint filed by Ghulam Nabi Magray on May 29, 2025, against the executive engineer, KPDCL, Handwara division, over alleged negligence in carrying forward outstanding dues from his former joint family house to his newly constructed residence.Magray had sought Rs 3 lakh in compensation for allegedly generating incorrect electricity bills, along with 10 percent interest and rectification of the bills. He had also sought Rs 1 lakh for mental agony and Rs 50,000 as litigation expenses.According to the complaint, Magray lived in a joint family house with his three brothers. He separated from the family in 1987 and shifted outside the Valley. He was the head of the joint family and the electricity connection for the shared house was registered in his name under Consumer ID No. 0214010006915.He would return to the Valley and reside temporarily with his sister, who resides at Keegam area of Kupwara.He later constructed a separate house and started residing there. However, he remained outside Kashmir for more than six months a year. The complainant alleged that despite the construction of his separate house, KPDCL “arbitrarily transferred the outstanding dues of the joint family house to his newly constructed residence instead of issuing an independent electricity bill.”He further alleged that the department continued generating bills for the new house despite the absence of basic electricity infrastructure, including electric poles and low-tension (LT) distribution lines near the premises. The outstanding amount had accumulated to Rs 2,10,934 by March 2025.Magray said he repeatedly approached the department seeking rectification of the bills and informing it that he had constructed a separate house but his requests went unheeded.After receiving notice from the commission, KPDCL appeared through its counsel but failed to file its written version within the stipulated period. Consequently, the commission closed the department's right to submit its reply.In its order, the commission observed that Magray had approached the department after constructing his new house and sought rectification of the electricity bills that continued to be generated in his name against the pre-existing jointly owned family house.It said although he had approached the deputy commissioner in 2018 and his representation had been forwarded to the executive engineer concerned, the bills continued to accumulate in his name. The commission said KPDCL was duty-bound to rectify the particulars of the electricity bills and issue them in the name of the proper subscriber of the jointly owned house instead of continuing to generate bills in Magray's name."Not rectifying the particulars of the electricity bills has accumulated the amount and has admittedly caused inconvenience to the complainant. Such inaction of the OP amounts to deficiency in service on the part of the OP," the commission observed.The commission quashed electricity bill No. 0214010006915 amounting to Rs 2,10,934 issued in Magray's name. It directed KPDCL to issue a fresh electricity bill in his name for the newly constructed house, provided the premises have an electricity connection. However, it clarified that Magray would remain liable to pay the outstanding dues against the jointly owned family house. The commission also directed KPDCL to pay him Rs 10,000 as litigation charges and comply with the order within two weeks of receiving a copy of it.
Article Summary: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission quashes electricity bill of Rs 2,10,934. The bill was issued by Kashmir Power Distribution Corporation Limited (KPDCL) The commission directed the KPDCL to issue a fresh bill for his newly constructed house and pay Rs 10,000 as litigation charges.

Article Title: India's ageing Barak missile shield gets Rs 1,976 crore upgrade: What changes
Article Text:
A Barak-1 missile being fired from an Israeli warship during a live fire drill. (Image credit: Israeli armed forces)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The defence ministry has signed a Rs 1,976.40 crore contract with Israel Aerospace Industries for the upgradation and obsolescence management of the Barak point defence missile system fitted on Indian warships. Under the deal, IAI will carry out a comprehensive overhaul of the system's hardware and software, which the ministry says will give naval platforms enhanced features and a potent anti-air defence capability.The announcement stresses capability, but obsolescence management is arguably the heart of the contract. The Barak-1 entered service around 2000 and has been deployed for over two decades on Delhi-class destroyers, Shivalik-class and Brahmaputra-class frigates and the aircraft carrier INS Vikramaditya. Many of its electronic components, processors and sensors are now ageing, and in several cases the original manufacturers no longer produce spares, making readiness increasingly expensive to sustain.Two practical considerations explain the need for modernisation of the point defence system. Replacing every installation would cost far more and disrupt operations more than upgrading systems already integrated into the fleet, and many of these ships will serve for years. DRDO 's indigenous VL-SRSAM is meant to succeed the Barak-1, but fleet-wide induction will take time.The upgrade ensures no capability gap in the interim. Better software, computing power and fire-control can improve reaction time, reliability, availability and resistance to jamming, even if the missile itself remains the same.The deal also underlines why point-defence systems matter. They form the last layer of an integrated air-defence network, protecting specific assets such as ships, airbases, radars and command centres against threats that slip past outer defences. On a warship, the Barak-1 is that final missile layer against aircraft, drones and anti-ship missiles. Warships are also equipped with gun based close in weapon systems such as the AK-630 which form the final line of defence.Cheap drones, loitering munitions and faster, low-flying missiles shorten reaction time, while the Russia-Ukraine conflict has shown how massed drones can be used against airbases and logistics hubs.Using costly long-range interceptors against inexpensive drones is an unfavourable trade, so shorter-range systems help conserve missiles for graver threats. The danger is saturation, where a defender runs out of interceptors even after intercepting everything.For India, with airbases and forward positions spread along the northern and western borders, layered cover is essential. DRDO's VSHORADS cleared three flight trials on February 27 this year, and the Integrated Air Defence Weapon System, combining QRSAM, VSHORADS and a laser-based weapon, had its maiden trials on August 23, 2025. The Defence Acquisition Council cleared VSHORADS and medium-range missile procurement for the Army on July 3.The Barak contract is thus less a missile purchase than a sustainment effort. It also reinforces the India-Israel defence partnership, which includes the jointly developed Barak-8.
Article Summary: India has signed a Rs 1,976.40 crore contract with Israel Aerospace Industries. IAI will carry out a comprehensive overhaul of the system's hardware and software. The Barak-1 entered service around 2000 and has been deployed for over two decades.

Article Title: After Akvan, another cyclonic circulation brewing in Bay: IMD
Article Text:
Mrutyunjay Mohapatra, IMD DG





BHUBANESWAR: Another cyclonic circulation is likely to develop over the Andaman Sea and southeast Bay of Bengal around Nov-end, the India Meteorological Department ( IMD ) said on Saturday, even as the remnant of Cyclone ‘Akvan’ weakened into a low-pressure area over interior Odisha This was also indicated in the IMD’s latest extended range forecast issued for two weeks, starting from Nov 19 till Dec 2.Mrutyunjay Mohapatra, IMD DG, said they have not issued any specific forecast regarding the exact location, intensity or trajectory of the possible system so far, except its mention in the extended range forecast.According to Mohapatra, four to five cyclones form in the Bay of Bengal from Oct to Dec. Three cyclones have already hit Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.The DG said the situation witnessed this year carries a lot of similarity with the strong El Niño year in 1987, and could be attributed to the El Niño factor.“It will be too early to predict more details about the possible system. People should keep a close watch on their upcoming bulletins,” he said.The IMD’s indication of the possible development of a fresh system has, however, raised concerns among people already hit hard by the recent cyclones.Meanwhile, under the influence of Cyclone Akvan, Bhograi in Balasore district received the state’s highest rainfall of 108 mm in the last 24 hours. Odagan in Nayagarh and Buguda in Ganjam followed, with 108.6 mm and 102 mm rainfall respectively.The engineer-in-chief of water resources department Dilip Rout said there was no threat of flood despite heavy rain in several southern and interior districts under the influence of Akvan in the last two days.
Article Summary: Another cyclonic circulation is likely to develop over the Andaman Sea and southeast Bay of Bengal around Nov-end. This was indicated in the IMD’s latest extended range forecast issued for two weeks, starting from Nov 19 till Dec 2. Three cyclones have already hit Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.
